scope: Research counterexamples for the proposed four-class source identity taxonomy only. This fixture does not define a source schema, resolver, loader, integrity executor, trust rule, closure rule, packet acceptance rule, integration behavior, epoch behavior, or replay behavior.

observed_repository_boundary.historical_artifact_source_refs: artifact schema v0.1/v0.2/v0.3 source_refs are unique non-empty opaque strings
observed_repository_boundary.historical_evidence_source_refs: evidence-record schema v0.1 source_refs are unique non-empty opaque strings
observed_repository_boundary.historical_non_reinterpretation: lexical shape must not upgrade historical source identity strength
observed_repository_boundary.proposal_separation: declared identity, existence, retrievability, integrity, provenance relation, trust/relevance, completeness/closure, and acceptance remain separate facts

cases.title: same historical token, different declaration occurrences
cases.attack: A future migration records only the token NEXT_BUILD.md and one newly grounded typed source identity, then treats that mapping as authority for both historical objects.
cases.expected_truth: The two historical declarations remain distinct occurrences even though the authored token text is equal. A migration must not collapse them by token equality.
cases.taxonomy_result: survives if opaque_label identity continues to include its containing historical object; future migration representation must exact-identify the declaration occurrence rather than token text alone

cases.title: composite pairing ambiguity
cases.attack: A future source view stores two locator facts and two content-address facts, then pairs them by array position, lexical order, resolver order, or recency.
cases.expected_truth: No locator-to-content association exists unless it is explicitly represented. All four facts remain independent otherwise.
cases.taxonomy_result: the four target classes remain sufficient, but any future composite declaration needs explicit association semantics; association is not a fifth target identity class

cases.title: same locator, different bytes over time
cases.attack: Locator equality is used to assert immutable source equality or to overwrite the earlier observed content identity.
cases.expected_truth: The locator remains one locator declaration while observations may disagree across time/context. Neither observation silently rewrites the other.
cases.taxonomy_result: survives; locator and content_address remain orthogonal

cases.title: same bytes, different locators
cases.attack: Different locator strings are used to infer different immutable content identity, or matching bytes are used to erase one locator declaration.
cases.expected_truth: Distinct locator declarations may point to identical bytes. Content equality does not erase locator/provenance distinctions.
cases.taxonomy_result: survives; declaration occurrences remain distinct even when a content target is shared

cases.title: exact AXM syntax without exact target availability
cases.attack: Canonical spelling alone is treated as target existence, integrity, currentness, or permission to substitute a same-logical-id object.
cases.expected_truth: Identity remains declared; retrievability is failed/unresolved. No logical-id, latest-version, storage-recency, or locator fallback is authorized.

cases.title: content digest without bytes and with mismatching bytes

candidate_states: bytes available but hash to sha256:B

cases.attack: Digest syntax or successful retrieval from a favored locator is treated as integrity success.
cases.expected_truth: Unavailable bytes leave integrity unresolved; mismatching bytes fail integrity. Resolver success cannot override either result.

cases.title: integrity laundering into trust or relevance
cases.attack: A valid digest match is treated as proof that the source is trustworthy, relevant, correct, sufficient, or acceptable.
cases.expected_truth: Integrity establishes byte identity only. Trust, relevance, correctness, sufficiency, and acceptance remain separate unresolved facts.

cases.title: all declared sources resolve but closure remains unknown
cases.attack: Successful retrieval of every declared source is treated as proof that the declaration set is complete or that evidence/packet acceptance follows.
cases.expected_truth: Retrieval success says nothing about omitted sources, closure, evidence precedence, packet acceptance, or integration.

cases.title: cross-field source laundering

neighboring_values: content_ref that looks like a digest

cases.attack: A neighboring field acquires source-provenance meaning because its spelling resembles one source identity class.
cases.expected_truth: Source authority exists only through an explicit source declaration/relation. Neighboring authored relations keep their own meaning.

cases.title: conflicting parallel typed declarations

setup.packet_or_lane_one: declares content_address sha256:A for source role X
setup.packet_or_lane_two: declares content_address sha256:B for source role X

cases.attack: Newest packet, schedule order, higher-confidence occupant, branch ownership, green CI, resolver preference, or Git permission selects one declaration as institutional truth.
cases.expected_truth: Both declarations remain explicit conflicting facts until a later grounded policy resolves them. No actor or execution fact becomes source-selection authority.

cases.title: exact AXM object and content address happen to cover equivalent bytes

setup.content_address: digest over bytes that happen to match an agreed byte scope of O

cases.attack: Byte equivalence automatically collapses the two declaration classes or invents a provenance/causal relation between them.
cases.expected_truth: The target identity facts may be correlated only through an explicit relation/verification statement. Class identity and provenance relation remain separate.
cases.taxonomy_result: survives; no fifth class is required

cases.title: offline replacement occupant reconstruction

setup.repository_state: contains historical object, typed declarations where present, and this adversarial fixture

cases.attack: The replacement occupant needs an undocumented parser, resolver preference, array pairing convention, or prior chat to decide source identity strength or declaration association.
cases.expected_truth: The occupant can recover each historical declaration at opaque strength and each future typed target by explicit class. Any association between declaration facts must be explicit; absent association stays unresolved.
cases.taxonomy_result: survives only if Decision 020 preserves explicit declaration-occurrence identity and never relies on implicit pairing conventions

adversarial_disposition.target_class_count: no counterexample found that requires splitting or adding a fifth source target identity class
adversarial_disposition.repair_guard: before a typed source-declaration contract is opened, preserve declaration occurrence identity and explicit association: equal tokens do not merge historical declarations, and separate locator/content/exact facts do not pair by position, recency, resolver order, actor identity, or infrastructure availability
adversarial_disposition.implementation_authority: none; this is research evidence only
